title: Minkowski's Inequality: Triangle Inequality for Lp Norms
content: This file answers the open question from `CauchySchwarzOQ03.lean`: **can Minkowski's inequality be derived from Hölder?** YES — the proof applies Hölder twice: write $\sum(f+g)^p = \sum(f+g)^{p-1} \cdot f + \sum(f+g)^{p-1} \cdot g$, apply Hölder to each sum with $h_i = (f+g)^{p-1}$, factor out $(\sum(f+g)^p)^{1/q}$, then divide.
mathContext: The **proof chain** in these files: Young ($ab \leq a^p/p + b^q/q$) → Hölder ($\sum fg \leq \|f\|_p \|g\|_q$) → Cauchy-Schwarz ($p=q=2$) → Minkowski ($\|f+g\|_p \leq \|f\|_p + \|g\|_p$) → $L^p$ is Banach. **Minkowski** (1896): proved while developing the geometry of numbers. **Riesz** (1910): systematized the Hölder-Minkowski duality — Hölder bounds pairings, Minkowski bounds norms; together they make $L^p$ a normed space whose dual is $L^q$.

title: Minkowski at p = 1: Linearity and Triangle Inequality
content: **minkowski_p1_nnreal**: For NNReal, $\sum_i (f_i + g_i) = \sum_i f_i + \sum_i g_i$ — one line: `Finset.sum_add_distrib`. **minkowski_p1_real**: For signed reals, $\sum_i |f_i + g_i| \leq \sum_i |f_i| + \sum_i |g_i|$ — by pointwise `abs_add` summed via `Finset.sum_le_sum`, then `sum_add_distrib`.
mathContext: The $p=1$ Minkowski inequality is the **classical triangle inequality for sums**. For NNReal it holds with equality (there are no negative values, so $|f+g| = f+g$). For signed reals, the triangle inequality $|a+b| \leq |a| + |b|$ is applied pointwise. The `calc` proof: $\sum |f_i + g_i| \leq \sum (|f_i| + |g_i|) = \sum |f_i| + \sum |g_i|$. `Finset.sum_le_sum` lifts pointwise inequalities to sum inequalities; `Finset.sum_add_distrib` splits sums over additions.

title: minkowski_nnreal: General Minkowski via Mathlib
content: **minkowski_nnreal**: For $p \geq 1$ and NNReal $f, g$: $(\sum_i (f_i+g_i)^p)^{1/p} \leq (\sum_i f_i^p)^{1/p} + (\sum_i g_i^p)^{1/p}$. One-line proof: `NNReal.Lp_add_le hp f g s`. This is the core Minkowski inequality — the entire file's purpose is to derive this and its corollaries.
mathContext: `NNReal.Lp_add_le` is Mathlib's Minkowski inequality for finite sums of NNReal values. Internally it proves Minkowski from Hölder: (1) expand $(f+g)^p = (f+g)^{p-1} \cdot (f+g)$; (2) bound by $(f+g)^{p-1} \cdot f + (f+g)^{p-1} \cdot g$; (3) apply Hölder to each with exponents $p, q = p/(p-1)$; (4) note $(p-1) \cdot q = p$ and cancel $(\sum(f+g)^p)^{1/q}$. The exponent $1/q = (p-1)/p$, so $1 - 1/q = 1/p$.

title: Minkowski for Signed Reals via NNReal Lift
content: **lp_sum_mono**: Monotonicity of Lp sums: if $h_i \leq k_i$ pointwise then $(\sum h_i^p)^{1/p} \leq (\sum k_i^p)^{1/p}$ for $p > 0$. Proved via `NNReal.rpow_le_rpow` and `Finset.sum_le_sum`. **minkowski_real**: For signed reals, $(\sum \|f_i+g_i\|_{\text{nn}}^p)^{1/p} \leq (\sum \|f_i\|_{\text{nn}}^p)^{1/p} + (\sum \|g_i\|_{\text{nn}}^p)^{1/p}$. Proof via `calc`: use `lp_sum_mono` with `nnnorm_add_le` to bound $\|f+g\|_{\text{nn}} \leq \|f\|_{\text{nn}} + \|g\|_{\text{nn}}$, then apply NNReal Minkowski.
mathContext: The **NNReal lift technique**: for signed reals, use `‖·‖₊` (nnnorm = non-negative norm) instead of `|·|`. The pointwise triangle inequality `nnnorm_add_le f g : ‖f + g‖₊ ≤ ‖f‖₊ + ‖g‖₊` reduces to the NNReal case. The `calc` chain: $(\sum \|f+g\|^p)^{1/p} \leq (\sum (\|f\|+\|g\|)^p)^{1/p}$ (by monotonicity + nnnorm triangle) $\leq (\sum \|f\|^p)^{1/p} + (\sum \|g\|^p)^{1/p}$ (by NNReal Minkowski).

title: Inner Product Space Triangle Inequality and Norm-Squared Bound
content: **minkowski_inner_product**: In any normed add comm group with inner product, $\|u+v\| \leq \|u\| + \|v\|$ — one line: `norm_add_le u v`. **norm_add_sq_le**: $\|u+v\|^2 \leq (\|u\|+\|v\|)^2$. Proof: just `nlinarith` from `minkowski_inner_product` and nonnegativity.
mathContext: In **inner product spaces**, the triangle inequality is an immediate consequence of Cauchy-Schwarz: expand $\|u+v\|^2 = \langle u+v, u+v \rangle = \|u\|^2 + 2\langle u,v \rangle + \|v\|^2 \leq \|u\|^2 + 2\|u\|\|v\| + \|v\|^2 = (\|u\|+\|v\|)^2$ (using CS). Mathlib bundles this into `norm_add_le`, so the proof is a one-liner. `norm_add_sq_le` is then obtained via `nlinarith` from the linear bound and nonnegativity — squaring both sides. The class requirements `[NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]` provide the abstract algebraic framework.

title: Integral Minkowski: Lp and L2 Triangle Inequalities
content: **minkowski_lp**: For Lp spaces ($p \geq 1$), $\|f+g\|_{L^p} \leq \|f\|_{L^p} + \|g\|_{L^p}$ — one line: `norm_add_le f g`. This holds because Mathlib's `Lp` type is a `NormedAddCommGroup`, so the triangle inequality is built in. **minkowski_l2**: Special case for $L^2(\mu)$ — same proof.
mathContext: Mathlib constructs `Lp ℝ p μ` as a `NormedAddCommGroup` for $p \geq 1$ (this requires the `[Fact (1 ≤ p)]` instance). The `norm_add_le` triangle inequality is then inherited from the group structure — Minkowski is **absorbed into the typeclass hierarchy**. This is a key design choice in Mathlib: rather than proving Minkowski as a separate theorem for integrals, it's a consequence of building `Lp` as a proper normed space. The `MeasureTheory.Lp` type uses `MeasureTheory.snorm` internally to define the norm.
relatedConcepts: Lp ℝ p μ as NormedAddCommGroup

title: Hölder-Minkowski Duality: Combined Statement
content: **holder_minkowski_chain**: For $p \geq 1$ with conjugate $q$ (so $1/p + 1/q = 1$): simultaneously (1) Hölder: $\sum f_i g_i \leq (\sum f_i^p)^{1/p} (\sum g_i^q)^{1/q}$ (via `NNReal.inner_le_Lp_mul_Lq`), and (2) Minkowski: $(\sum(f_i+g_i)^p)^{1/p} \leq (\sum f_i^p)^{1/p} + (\sum g_i^p)^{1/p}$ (via `NNReal.Lp_add_le`). Both in one `⟨..., ...⟩` pair.
mathContext: **Hölder-Minkowski duality**: Hölder says the $L^q$ norm bounds the $L^p$ functional ($\langle \cdot, g \rangle_{L^p}$), while Minkowski says $L^p$ is closed under addition (triangle inequality). Together: $L^p$ is a normed space with dual $L^q$. `Real.HolderConjugate q p` is the Mathlib predicate encoding $1/p + 1/q = 1$. The combined statement serves as a pedagogical summary: the entire Young-Hölder-Minkowski chain in a single theorem asserting the two fundamental inequalities for conjugate exponents.
